title: Most Investors Fear Uncertainty, But Systematic Traders Don’t - Systematic Investor - Ep. 406

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Most Investors Fear Uncertainty, But Systematic Traders Don’t - Systematic Investor - Ep. 406.docx

summary: Rzepczynski and Kaastrup-Larsen review H1 2026 trend following (profits concentrated in oil, gold and dollar reversals) and the new Fed chair as a structural regime change. Mark's study: hedge fund excess returns and alpha deteriorate in high-VIX regimes while managed futures is insensitive with negative beta.

coverage.note: intro, World Cup banter, Greenspan death and Fed history
Greenspan vs today, 1994, Fed chair equity returns
Fed chair data, Hormuz and Brent, June numbers, trend concentration
gold, dollar and bond moves, number of markets debate
heating oil vs crude, correlation, topic plan
NLP/LLMs, Warsh dovish expectations, Fed politics
five Fed task forces: guidance, balance sheet, data, productivity
effect on trend followers, balance sheet
AI productivity, monetary regime, economic trend, blend weights
hedge fund risk regime study design
betas, regime bins, managed futures insensitive
risk shocks, alpha, beta by regime
allocation conclusion, equity market neutral, wrap-up

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader covered the Fed-chair, trend-concentration and VIX-regime study ideas well; missed side arguments (Fed communication history, bank bond buying, profit-motive pricing, data-integrity concerns, global macro result, host's corroboration) and the Great Moderation framing.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: it's at at key periods of time, a single person could have a huge influence on the economy
claims.claim: Individual central bankers matter at key moments, e.g. Greenspan in 1994 hurt mortgage portfolios.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: he was not able to identify or accept that there was a bubble after he lowered interest rates, you know, to close to 1% which really sort of exploded the housing market
claims.claim: Greenspan's cuts to about 1 percent fed the housing bubble that led to the financial crisis.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it came kind of a bit of out of the out of the blue and it was not well received initially by trend following managers
claims.claim: The surprise first rate hike in about 5 years in 1994 was initially bad for trend followers.
claims.conditions: sudden policy shift after long pause

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I don't see any of these where the equity market has actually gone up
claims.claim: Barclays/Bloomberg data: S&P fell in the first 3 months of each new Fed chair (Greenspan -33%, Powell -7%, Yellen -4%, Bernanke -2%).
claims.testable: yes: event study of Fed chair changes

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: What it's meant is that Brent now trades at 4-month lows.
claims.claim: Hormuz normalisation took Brent to 4-month lows, a regime change in energy that pressured June 2026 trend-following performance.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Equities and some of the metals I think have had some meaningful corrections this month.
claims.claim: June 2026 had corrections in equities, metals (silver about -19 percent) and energy, while the US dollar strengthened.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: The beta 50 is flat for the month, but still up 9.67 for the year.
claims.claim: Named data: SG CTA and Trend indices up about 10.6-10.9 percent YTD, Beta50 +9.67 percent; MSCI World +8.26 percent, S&P TR +8.22 percent.
claims.indicator: SG CTA; SG Trend; Beta50; MSCI World

correction.issue: Index names are inferred, not stated: the transcript (captions) says 'short term trend index' for the two figures (+10.88 and +10.6 YTD) and gives a third, the 'short term traders index', at about +5.5 percent YTD, which is omitted; the Beta50 and MSCI/S&P figures are right.
correction.fix: Named YTD data as read out (June 2026): trend-type CTA indices up about 10.9 and 10.6 percent (captioned 'short term trend index', likely SG CTA/SG Trend), the short term traders index up about 5.5 percent, Beta50 up 9.67 percent, MSCI World up 8.26 percent and S&P 500 total return up 8.22 percent; trend followers beat both equities and the short-term traders index.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if you look back over a given year, most of the money will be only made in a few markets
claims.claim: Trend-following profits concentrate in a few markets each year (a dirty secret of diversification).

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: whether you were a profitable or very profitable CTA right down this year was whether you could be able to exploit the run up, be able to then manage the risk at at the turnaround
claims.claim: In H1 2026 oil ran up at the start of the Iran conflict then reversed; the best CTAs rode the run-up and managed risk at the turn.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you look at we've gone from like 5,200 down to, you know, now we're close to 4,000
claims.claim: Gold fell from about 5,200 to 4,000 and the dollar went from falling to a strong uptrend, the opposite of what the world conflict implied.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the 10-year has been trading between 4 4 and 1/2 4 middle almost a a year
claims.claim: US 10-year yields stayed range-bound between 4 and 4.5 percent for about a year, offering no trend; performance came from lesser markets.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: I don't know which market is going to have this big move. So I need to trade a larger basket
claims.claim: Trade a broad market set because the big winning market is unknown in advance.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if I trade too large a basket or if my position if I don't manage my positions carefully then what will happen is is that I capture those right markets, but I don't have enough of it
claims.claim: Too many markets dilute exposure to the winners; hence a middle ground that also preserves liquidity.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: as soon as you step into the arena uh and you want to trade your own trend-following um system those rules don't work
claims.claim: Regression replicators can express exposure with 10-12 markets, but running a real trend system needs a much broader set for risk and opportunity.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: So, you left something on the table by only trading crude oil in this instance.
claims.claim: Over 12 months crude rose 37 percent but heating oil 130 percent, so related contracts in a sector can hold the bigger move.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you actually like when markets start to get correlated because then it increases uh uh the the uh the shock effect from uh from a given shock
claims.claim: Trend followers want correlations to rise in a shock so positions in crude, Brent, heating oil and RBOB multiply gains.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you don't care about whether it's positive or negatively correlated. All you care about is the absolute correlation.
claims.claim: Only the absolute correlation matters for trend followers, as long or short positions both profit from shocks.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: what you want to look at is is that are there going to be regime changes or dislocations in the market that could lead to longer-term trends
claims.claim: For allocating to managed futures, look for regime changes or dislocations that start longer-term trends.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: A structural change, which we're going to talk about, would be a change in the in in the head of the the Fed.
claims.claim: Structural regime changes (a new Fed chair stamping policy) can create new trends or reversals, as opposed to behavioural responses to shocks.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if you have a regime where there's high uncertainty, then there's going to be more caution in behavior. If there's more cautious in behavior, then the price adjustment to a new equilibrium will take time
claims.claim: High uncertainty makes investors dollar-cost-average, slowing price adjustment and creating trends.
claims.testable: yes: trend returns by uncertainty regime

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: they're trying to now convert soft information into numerical information or hard information
claims.claim: NLP/LLMs convert earnings calls and Fed text into numerical signals, changing how markets react to announcements.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: it doesn't seem that he's as dovish a Fed chairman as what was been perceived
claims.claim: Chair Warsh was expected to be dovish and less independent, but Mark thinks he is less dovish.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if we get to 4% inflation, the Fed is probably going to raise rates. If if we get below 3% inflation, then there's going to be the drumbeat to that we should actually lower rates
claims.claim: In practice the Fed runs a 3-4 percent inflation range rather than 2 percent: hikes near 4 and cuts below 3.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the politics of the Fed is much more complex. Yes, it's the executive versus the the Fed executive branch. But there's also the politics between Wall Street and Main Street.
claims.claim: Fed politics has three layers: executive versus Fed, Wall Street versus Main Street, and internal dissent.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: Chairman Warsh is not a fan of forward guidance
claims.claim: Warsh gives no dot and signals dot plots are in pencil, so forward guidance is likely cut back.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if you don't have an accommodative Fed with a large balance sheet, then that means that the federal debt in the US is going to have to be financed from other sources
claims.claim: A smaller Fed balance sheet means Treasury debt is financed by private or reserve buyers, changing bond-market dynamics.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the quality of data that's being introduced into the marketplace from the US sources is not as good as what it has been in the past
claims.claim: US data quality is falling (low survey response), which favours price-based over fundamental systems.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: he was the one who probably really noted that there was a productivity boom in the 1990s
claims.claim: An AI productivity boom could allow looser monetary policy, as Greenspan did in the 1990s.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: macro trends will drive price trends. Hence, you want to look at fundamentals to be able to give you a support or another indication on what will be the direction of prices
claims.claim: Mark is a trend follower plus fundamentalist: macro trends drive price trends, so fundamentals corroborate direction.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: less forward guidance may be good for trend followers. It's going to mean that prices aren't going to be as noisy going forward.
claims.claim: Less Fed speech makes prices less noisy and driven by fundamentals, benefiting trend following.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: a single player is not going to drive prices. It will now be driven by the supply and demand across all agents within the marketplace
claims.claim: A shrinking Fed balance sheet improves price discovery, favouring trend following.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the market clearing price may be you know in in this case the rates are going to be higher
claims.claim: If the Fed stops buying, someone else must, and the clearing yield is higher.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the value of the person who just focuses on price is probably is going to be more valuable in this in a poor data environment
claims.claim: With poor data, quasi-fundamental value falls and pure price-based trading becomes more valuable.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we found out there was less jobs and then and these are major revisions
claims.claim: Large BLS revisions make fundamental reactions hard; economic-data trend models face data-reliability risk.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: Fed policy is not conducive to price stability
claims.claim: Inflation has been above 2 percent for 5+ years though Bernanke and Yellen feared deflation.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: We'll say it's neutral in in effect on how it affects trend followers.
claims.claim: AI productivity effect on trend following is neutral/unclear, though it could lift growth.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the big structural regime change is going to be in monetary policy
claims.claim: The key H2 2026 regime change is monetary policy under the new chair, though not immediately visible in P&L; early months could be negative.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the confidence numbers and survey data, this is not a very strong economy
claims.claim: Weak confidence and survey data (consumer confidence near 2020 levels, high inflation expectations) cast doubt on the second-half equity rally.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you systematically weight the two of them, then the combination will uh be better. You'll have you'll lower volatility and have a smoother, you know, return pattern.
claims.claim: Combining a price-based and fundamental system with systematic weights lowers volatility and smooths returns.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the weighting on the fundamental system has been uh lower than what I've seen in the past when I look at at models
claims.claim: As data quality declines optimised weights move toward the price-based system.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: how are they sensitive to uh risk. Not in terms of systematic risk like their beta, but how do they look at risk in as a measure of uncertainty through let's say the VIX index
claims.claim: Study design: measure hedge fund strategy sensitivity to risk regime (VIX level) and risk shocks (VIX change), separate from beta.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if they're skilled portfolio managers, they should do a pretty good job of being able to, you know, handle this kind of uh kind of risk
claims.claim: Null hypothesis: skilled managers' returns are independent of risk regime and shocks.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of them are actually they have a lot of similarities, very high correlation when things get difficult uh in in equity land
claims.claim: Many hedge fund strategies are correlated and negatively skewed in equity stress, trend following is the opposite.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the beta for managed futures is close to zero
claims.claim: Managed futures beta is close to zero; other strategies are between 0 and 1.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: like fixed income arb, uh there's a negative sensitivity to the risk regime
claims.claim: Arbitrage strategies such as fixed income arb are hurt by high-volatility regimes.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if we look at a high risk regime, uh you know, excess returns diminish significantly
claims.claim: Binned regressions: low/medium risk shows no sensitivity but in high VIX regimes hedge fund excess returns drop significantly after beta.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: in high-risk regimes, there's no sensitivity to manage futures
claims.claim: Managed futures excess returns are unaffected by high VIX regimes, with near-zero beta.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: Managed futures is insensitive to high risk shocks.
claims.claim: Most hedge fund strategies have negative coefficients to VIX shocks; managed futures is indifferent.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: in a high risk regimes, the alpha that you thought was positive for many strategies turns negative
claims.claim: Positive alpha of event-driven, market neutral and convertible arb turns negative in high-risk regimes; managed futures has no alpha component.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: your beta actually gets more negative for managed futures in high risk regimes and high risk shocks
claims.claim: Managed futures beta becomes negative in high-risk regimes and shocks, while other strategies' betas rise.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: You should probably increase your allocation to managed futures
claims.claim: If expecting high uncertainty/VIX, increase managed futures allocation.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: a big shock to uh to the VIX index, you know, and that was sort of correlated when the performance for managed futures actually improved
claims.claim: Anecdotally, a recent VIX spike coincided with better managed futures performance, but one case cannot be extrapolated.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: they might do a little bit better in some in some environments
claims.claim: Equity market neutral may do slightly better in some shock environments.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if you're trying to sort of protect yourself against uh you know, risk high risk regimes and risk shocks, that's may not be the best strategy
claims.claim: A bundle of alternative strategies does not protect against high-risk regimes; pick managed futures.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: great moderation, um where we had a long stretch of low inflation and steady economic growth
claims.claim: The Greenspan era (late 1980s to 2006) is remembered as the Great Moderation, a long stretch of low inflation and steady growth that ran almost to the financial crisis, and the crisis is linked by many to the Fed's policy in the run-up.
claims.testable: partly - volatility regimes can be measured, causal link to Fed policy is narrative

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Now Walsh, interestingly enough, is kind of moving towards the the Greenspan or maybe the pre-Greenspan era in terms of not really wanting to to share too much
claims.claim: Fed communication went from a statement of a couple of hundred words in 1994 to meeting notes, projections and press conferences; the new chair is moving back toward minimal communication and no forecasts, a reversal of the transparency regime.
claims.indicator: Fed communication volume (statement, SEP, press conference)
claims.testable: partly - communication regime change dates are observable, market effect is not tested here

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the academics validate what the central bank is doing. And so they'll they'll sort of say that yes, what they do make sense from our perspective. That doesn't mean it's good policy.
claims.claim: A fourth layer of Fed politics is the academics, whose models validate whatever the central bank does; this validation shows internal consistency, not that the policy is good, so academic support is weak evidence of sound policy.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it has also become very much in vogue to talk about economic trend where you look actually at economic data and it's been doing very well for those who have done that the last couple of years
claims.claim: Trend models built on economic data (rather than prices) have done very well in the last couple of years and have become fashionable, so their exposure to data-quality changes matters.
claims.conditions: performance is recent; data-quality changes may break it
claims.testable: partly - needs a defined economic-trend strategy and track record

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: A trend follower will say that that I just need to look at the prices themselves. The other information may be more backward-looking or it doesn't update it as quickly.
claims.claim: The pure price-trend argument against fundamentals is that macro information is backward-looking and updates slowly, so prices already carry the useful information; Mark sees a middle ground where fundamentals corroborate price trends.
claims.testable: yes - compare price-only and price-plus-fundamental trend systems

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: forward guidance may have served a purpose when we are at the the zero bound. But, now we'll sort of say that it's the actions that should drive prices and drive markets.
claims.claim: Forward guidance was useful at the zero lower bound but now actions should drive prices, so diminishing its importance removes speech-driven noise from market prices.
claims.conditions: effective at the zero bound; less needed once rates are above zero
claims.testable: partly - event-study of price noise around Fed communication

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it, i.e. the banks, somehow with some kind of rule uh that, you know, makes it more um tenable for banks to own more bonds and whatever.
claims.claim: If the Fed steps back from buying Treasuries it may push banks to become the buyer through regulatory rules, so the identity of the owner may matter less than the fact that heavy debt supply still has to be absorbed.
claims.indicator: Treasury issuance; bank Treasury holdings; bank capital rules
claims.testable: partly - bank holdings and issuance are observable, rule changes are not specified

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: we would like to have the people who buy or sell bonds are doing it because they have clear profit objectives.
claims.claim: Bond prices are more informative when the marginal buyers and sellers are profit-motivated rather than driven by policy or regulation, which is the market structure that favours trend followers and price discovery.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: that's good because then you're going to reduce the noise and you're going to and you're going to increase the link between the economics and and prices
claims.claim: In the long run better official data reduces noise and tightens the link between economic fundamentals and prices, which would help data-driven systems, even though poor data hurts them in the short run.
claims.conditions: long run only; short run the data quality is poor
claims.testable: partly - measure data-signal predictive power before and after revisions

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I'm always kind of concerned that there probably is a motivation in terms of changing the way data is collected and what data is even collected.
claims.claim: Changes to what official data is collected and how may be motivated by making the data look better, which is a data-integrity risk for fundamental and economic-trend systems and a reason to trust prices more.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: productivity is is is going to be important for the global growth because right now global growth is is relatively poor.
claims.claim: Global growth is currently relatively weak, so a productivity boom from AI would matter for fundamental prices more than for trend followers directly.
claims.testable: partly - productivity and growth series exist

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you can think of competition within your industry, but if let's say that there are players outside your industry that might have an impact on your business
claims.claim: An allocator chooses among more than ten hedge fund strategies, so managed futures should be evaluated against the whole strategy universe, not only against other CTAs.
claims.testable: yes - cross-strategy comparison on common data

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: obviously you can be the right on the right side with your uh with your tail risk strategy, but in my favorite would of course be something like trend following
claims.claim: In high-risk regimes tail-risk strategies are on the right side, but the host prefers trend following as the diversifier for a high-VIX environment.
claims.direction: long trend following or tail risk in high-VIX regimes

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: Now, the same also applies to global macro, but the coefficient is negative.
claims.claim: Global macro, like managed futures, shows an insignificant sensitivity to the high-risk regime but with a negative coefficient, so it should be given less weight as a high-VIX diversifier.
claims.indicator: global macro hedge fund excess return vs VIX regime
claims.testable: yes - regression on hedge fund indices

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the case of managed futures trend following it's been pretty solid 12 months
claims.claim: The past 12 months were unusually uncertain, and managed futures trend following had a solid year, consistent with the regime finding.
claims.indicator: managed futures performance over the last 12 months

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: there's more likely that there's going to be some disconnect uh that there's going to be some uh change in the environment so that so that your strategy may not be as effective
claims.claim: Long-short and structured strategies fail in high-volatility regimes because relationships they rely on disconnect and the environment changes, which explains the negative alpha found in those regimes.
claims.indicator: long-short and structured trade performance in high vol
claims.testable: partly - the study shows the effect, not the mechanism

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: We did some analysis on our side at Dawn also in a similar vein in terms of analyzing different alternative investment strategies versus trend following and and and obviously we come to to similar conclusions.
claims.claim: The host's own firm analysis of alternative strategies versus trend following reached similar conclusions to Mark's VIX-regime study, which is independent supporting evidence.
